messages:
Diego: Hi payroll team — noticed my Dec pay has a retro salary adjustment processed in USD then converted to ARS, and the withholding lines look wrong (very high). Did we apply non-resident rates by mistake?
Sofia: Did you change your tax residency this year? That can trigger different withholding profiles.
Diego: No, still resident in ARS. I submitted address/doc updates back in March.
Mariana (Payroll): Thanks for flagging. Can you share the paystub PDF and the case number if you already opened one?
Diego: Uploaded paystub to a case now: PR-2026-721. Payline shows "Retro Adj USD 400 -> ARS 1,120,000 gross; Withheld ARS 560,000" (48% withholding)
Tomas (TaxOps): Sounds like the retro pay hit the global supplemental path and the system applied the foreigner/non-resident table for payroll runs that used the USD pay element. We'll need to check the element mapping and whether currency conversion was done before tax calc.
Mariana (Payroll): Action items: Diego please attach the bank FX confirmation and the original salary change email. We'll audit the payroll run for Dec and Jan. If withholding is incorrect, we'll do a correcting entry in the next run and submit remittance adjustments with AFIP.
PeopleOps Bot: Case PR-2026-721 created and assigned to intl-tax. ETA initial triage 4 business days.
Diego: Thanks — will add FX proof. One question: will this affect my personal annual sworn statement with AFIP?
Tomas (TaxOps): If we correct withholding before year-end filings, we should be able to issue corrected payslips; otherwise you may receive updated certificates to use when preparing your annual return. We'll coordinate on documentation for AFIP.
Mariana (Payroll): We'll keep you posted here once triage is done. For KB purposes, we should add a note about retro adjustments + currency conversion causing incorrect non-resident withholding.
Sofia: Good idea — people-ops can add a short checklist for retro pay in foreign currency.
Diego: Appreciate it. Leaving this open until fixed.
